correctness.rationale: The substitution h(a)=ab,h(b)=ac,h(c)=db,h(d)=dc and coding a,b→0,c,d→1 generate the digit-defined Rudin–Shapiro sequence. The eight alternating substitution triples occur in h^8(a); for each h(x)=pq both h^{k-1}(p)h^{k-1}(q)h^{k-1}(p) and its QPQ converse occur, so all 2^k rotations of W_k(x) are factors. The four W_1 blocks 00,01,10,11 are distinct and injectivity lifts to each level; different halves imply W_k(x) primitive for k>=2 (every nonprimitive power of 2 length repeats its two halves). Their one-count vector plus wrap-around 0100 count is invariant under rotation. Explicit w_even/w_odd recurrences and the k→k+2 q-matrix distinguish each of the four entries for k>=3. Independent direct-digit factors verify every rotation up to k=8, and recurrences/distinct invariants k=3..10. These finite cases are not the all-k proof; substitution and induction supply it.
